_comment: TREATMENT ARM for the pop-need weight experiment: VANILLA + TELEMETRY + THIS FILE'S ONE CHANGE AND NOTHING ELSE. No buildings, no production methods, no history, no localization. Its control is the plain {kind: control} runs of the SAME schedule. Do NOT add industries or any other key here - the entire value of this arm is that it differs from vanilla in exactly one file. The multipliers match config/mod_config.x10.json so the two experiments are comparable, except that this one is not confounded by the tier split.
_arm_naming: ⚠ THIS IS NOT A CONTROL ARM. It is currently BUILT by one - {kind: control, config: <this file>} - and that is a known architectural violation, flagged in CLAUDE.md under -ControlOnly and to be fixed before the next commit to build.ps1. A control varies NOTHING but its telemetry; an arm carrying a gameplay file is a small mod and must be named like one. When the fix lands this becomes {kind: overlay, config: <this file>} and build_state.json records arm 'overlay+pop_needs'. Sessions run 2026-08-05/06 record 'control+pop_needs'; read that as overlay, and do not back-fill their build_state.json.
_why_luxury_furniture_matters: FINDINGS F35: no pop need in the game has an observable budget - all 15 share a good with another need - so the LEVEL of a good's share can never identify the allocation rule and only a perturbation can. popneed_luxury_items is the single exception while it lasts: silk, luxury_clothes, luxury_furniture and porcelain are each single-need and none is a 'local' good, so its budget IS observable until radios are invented. luxury_furniture also trades from 1836, so it answers in the first minutes of a run. It is the cleanest venue in the game for this experiment; steamers (popneed_leisure, 9 goods) and automobiles (two needs at once) are far messier and are along for the ride.
